descriptions.text: Improper verification mechanism for assigning the "premarket user" role. The system only checks if the transfer amount equals the balance of the teamWalletAddress, which is public information and easily exploitable. Vulnerable code snippet: https://vscode.blockscan.com/base/0x7f12d13b34f5f4f0a9449c16bcd42f0da47af200 Attack tx: https://app.blocksec.com/explorer/tx/base/0xa618933a0e0ffd0b9f4f0835cc94e523d0941032821692c01aa96cd6f80fc3fd Analysis: https://extropy-io.medium.com/block-forensics-an-in-depth-analysis-of-the-normie-memecoin-incident-0daf5baed08b

According to community feedback, the Base ecosystem's meme coin NORMIE has been attacked. The attacker exploited a design flaw in the NORMIE token's cross-chain bridge, manipulating the price on the Base Chain using flash loans. Since transactions with NORMIE on the Base Chain incur taxes, these taxes are automatically directed to a wallet controlled by the project team. The attacker injected a large amount of funds into this wallet via flash loans, significantly diluting the token's supply and causing a flash crash in the price.

On 26 May 2024, the NORMIE token contract on Base suffered a logic exploit that enabled an attacker to mint hundreds of millions of tokens, collapse the market cap by over 99%, and extract more than $880,000 in ETH. The attack exploited a flawed authorization condition on a privileged role (premarket_user) and a hidden minting pathway inside _transfer(). The NORMIE token contract assigned the powerful premarket_user role to any address that received a token transfer equal to the team wallet's balance.
